  `published_fiber_routes`, `osm_telecom_lines`, `interstates`.
- `data/us_fiber_by_state.gpkg`: the two fiber layers combined and split into''','''- `data/us_fiber_network.gpkg`: one layer per source:
  `published_fiber_routes`, `carrier_map_files`, `osm_telecom_lines`, `interstates`.
- `data/us_fiber_by_state.gpkg`: the three fiber layers combined and split into'''),
("`--only osm|published|interstates` rebuilds one layer.","`--only published|files|osm|interstates` rebuilds one layer."),
('''| `osm_telecom_lines` |''','''| `carrier_map_files` | KMZ/GeoPDF files carriers publish on their own websites ([`sources/carrier_files.py`](sources/carrier_files.py)) | US Signal and Midwest Fiber Networks (KMZs their website maps load), plus Southern Telecom (GeoPDFs, extracted by [`tools/extract_geopdf.py`](tools/extract_geopdf.py) into a committed GeoJSON). |
| `osm_telecom_lines` |'''),
('''## How published layers are chosen
''','''## Leads from Infrapedia

[Infrapedia](https://www.infrapedia.com/) is a good terrestrial network atlas,
but it can't be used as a source: the map needs a LinkedIn login and its FAQ
says the data can't be downloaded. Its public sitemap
(`infrapedia.com/terrestrialnetworks.xml`, allowed by its robots.txt) does list
the ~220 networks it shows, though, and Infrapedia's data mostly comes from the
operators themselves. So each US network on that list was traced back to its
operator's own website map:

- **Traceable to downloadable data** (in this build): Uniti/Windstream (the
  ArcGIS map embedded on unitiwholesale.com), FiberLight (ArcGIS map on
  fiberlight.com), US Signal (KMZs), Southern Telecom (GeoPDFs), and Unite
  Private Networks (via Kansas City's public right-of-way layers). Tracing also
  turned up an FDOT District 7 project that publishes surveyed utilities by owner.
  These are in [`sources/carrier_maps.py`](sources/carrier_maps.py) and
  [`sources/carrier_files.py`](sources/carrier_files.py).
- **Not traceable** (static image/PDF only, sales-gated, or no public map):
  WOW Business, Cox, Charter/Spectrum, Crown Castle/Lightower, ExteNet, Zayo,
  Arcadian Infracom, MOX, Transtelco, EarthLink, Edison Carrier Solutions, 123NET,
  Windstream's old KMZ page (now a 404).
- **Found but not used:** a public ArcGIS account named `geocode_Zayo` with
  ~200k Zayo fiber spans including strand counts and availability. It has no
  organization or profile, so it can't be verified as Zayo's own. It looks like
  internal operational data, and it falls under the Zayo rule anyway.

## How published layers are chosen
'''),
]
for a,b in reps:
    assert s.count(a)==1,a[:50]; s=s.replace(a,b)
p.write_text(s,encoding="utf-8"); print("ok")
EOF

# Decisions log

Newest on top.

## 2026-09-24 — US fiber route collector: provenance rule, no railroads, data not in git

- **What:** `scripts/us-fiber-network/` gathers publicly published US fiber *route*
  geometry (mostly ArcGIS layers from cities, counties, DOTs, utilities, carriers, plus
  OpenStreetMap) and splits it by state. The output feeds the "State & Regional Fiber
  Networks" group in Vy's thesis QGIS project as `<State> (compiled)` layers.
- **Provenance rule:** keep public entities + carriers publishing their own network;
  drop consultants, Esri demo data, anonymous uploads, and Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle routes
  not published by that carrier. Vy picked this over "public only" and "everything". It
  matches the thesis log's earlier calls (Lumen's no-duplication terms, rejecting an
  untraceable Pennsylvania re-upload, rejecting Vermont's availability-snapped "routes").
  Excluded layers stay in the committed catalog CSV with a reason, so the rule can be
  revisited without re-running discovery.
- **Railroads left out** at Vy's request, even though a lot of long-haul fiber follows
  rail. Interstates are still collected as a context layer but aren't added to the map.
- **Generated data is git-ignored.** It's 1–2 GB, far past what belongs in a public
  Pages repo. The committed catalog makes a rebuild reproducible; the thesis copy lives
  in Vy's thesis folder.
- **Ruled out:** InterTubes and FiberLocator (gated/licensed), PeeringDB (AUP), Infrapedia
  (login plus no downloads). See the thesis methodology log for details.

## 2026-09-10 — Enabled entire.io CLI to capture AI session history in git

- **What:** Installed the [entire](https://entire.io) CLI and ran `entire enable`, which
  hooked into Claude Code (via `.claude/settings.json` hooks) and started capturing AI
  coding sessions as git refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/...`) linked to commits. Added
  read-only `entire` subcommands (`status`, `session`, `checkpoint`, `blame`, `why`,
  `recap`, `doctor`, `version`) to the permission allowlist so they don't prompt.
- **Why:** Requested so anyone reading this repo's history later — Vy, the SWE, or a
  future Claude session — can see not just *what* changed but the actual AI session
  that produced it, without relying on chat transcripts living elsewhere.
- **Privacy tradeoff, explicitly accepted:** by default, checkpoints sync to `origin`
  alongside code (`entire status` confirms "Checkpoints sync to: origin"). HELP-ME is
  **public**, so this means captured AI session content (prompts, tool calls) becomes
  publicly visible in git history, not just the code. This was flagged before enabling
  and the call was made deliberately to let checkpoints go public rather than route
  them to a separate private remote. If that changes, checkpoint routing is reconfigured
  via `entire configure`, not by disabling capture entirely.
- **Not yet done:** `entire login` (browser OAuth to a hosted Entire account) — that's a
  one-time human step neither I nor a future session can complete on someone else's
  behalf. Local checkpoint capture works without it; login only gates hosted features
  (cross-repo `entire activity`, semantic `entire search`, etc.).

## 2026-09-10 — Repo set up as a GitHub Pages site with worktree + PR workflow

- **What:** Made the repo public, turned on GitHub Pages (source: `main` branch, root),
  and laid out folders: site content at the repo root (`index.html`, `css/`, `js/`,
  `assets/`, `pages/`), non-site tooling under `scripts/`, and this `docs/` folder for
  memory/rationale.
- **Why:** Repo previously had no structure (a loose script + gif at root) and Pages
  wasn't enabled. The site is meant to be one page reachable at one URL, navigated via
  tabs (see `js/main.js`), not a folder-per-project layout — so the root stays the
  site's home and `docs/` is reserved purely for this log rather than doubling as the
  Pages source.
- **Workflow going forward:** feature work happens on a branch (via a git worktree),
  pushed early via a PR, reviewed by the SWE before merging to `main`. No unit tests
  required (not production software) but changes should be manually verified — opened
  in a browser, script run once — before pushing. Keep commits small and the message
  focused on *why*.
- **Moved:** `ascii_network_animation.py` + `panopticon_network.gif` → `scripts/ascii-network-animation/`
  and `assets/` respectively; the GIF is now shown on the site's Projects tab as an
  example entry.

Add operator-published fiber traced from Infrapedia's network list

Infrapedia is a useful reference, but its map needs a login and its terms
rule out downloads. Its public sitemap still lists the terrestrial networks
it shows, and that data mostly comes from the operators. Tracing each US
network to the operator's own website map found downloadable data for:

- Uniti/Windstream: the public ArcGIS layers behind unitiwholesale.com's
  map (national core, regional transport, dark fiber, ~700k segments). This
  also proves the "anonymous" dark fiber layer from the first sweep is
  Uniti's own.
- FiberLight: its national network layer.
- US Signal and Midwest Fiber Networks: KMZs their website maps load
  (skipping an MWFN file labelled "nda").
- Southern Telecom: GeoPDFs, extracted by pen colour with QGIS's GDAL into
  a committed GeoJSON, since the pip GDAL has no PDF driver.
- Kansas City's right-of-way fiber layers (incl. Unite Private Networks)
  and an FDOT D7 project's surveyed telecom utilities.

Also fixes the electric-layer filter, which matched the "elec" in
"telecom" and had wrongly dropped three telecom layers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin claude/infrapedia-leads 2>&1 | tail -1

## What

Adds fiber route data traced from the US networks listed on Infrapedia, plus a filter bug fix.

**Not traceable:** WOW, Cox, Charter, Crown Castle/Lightower, ExteNet, Zayo, Arcadian, MOX, Transtelco, EarthLink, Edison, 123NET.

**New in `sources/carrier_maps.py`** (seeded into the ArcGIS catalog, publisher preset):
- Uniti: the layers behind unitiwholesale.com's map, roughly 700k segments.
- FiberLight's national network layer.
- Kansas City right-of-way layers, including Unite Private Networks.
- FDOT D7 Westshore project: surveyed telecom utilities.

**New in `sources/carrier_files.py`** (new build layer `carrier_map_files`):
- US Signal: 12 state KMZs.
- Midwest Fiber Networks: the KMZ labelled "website".
- Southern Telecom: GeoPDF fiber via `tools/extract_geopdf.py`, output committed as GeoJSON.

**Bug fix:** the electric-layer regex matched the "elec" in "t**elec**om", which dropped 3 telecom layers.

## Why

Vy uses Infrapedia as a reference and asked for its sources, restricted to terrestrial lines. Infrapedia itself isn't usable: the map needs a login and its FAQ says there are no downloads. So only its public sitemap's network names were used, each traced to the operator's own website map. Judgment calls are in `docs/DECISIONS.md`:
- A public "geocode_Zayo" account with strand-level data is skipped because it can't be verified as Zayo's.
- An MWFN KMZ with "nda" in its filename is skipped.

## Verified

- **Full build.** 632/632 catalog layers downloaded with no failures, plus 18,412 features from carrier map files; the by-state split produced 52 states/territories.
- **GeoPDF placement.** Each Southern Telecom GeoPDF was checked by bounding box and lands in its named city.
- **In QGIS.** Merged into Vy's thesis project, 1,406,267 features across 52 state layers. A screenshot shows new coverage in the right places: Southeast from Uniti/Kinetic, Midwest from US Signal.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
Your map now has about twice as much fiber: 1,406,267 line segments across 52 state layers, up from about 673,000. The biggest gains are the Southeast and the Midwest, and South Dakota has data for the first time. It's all US terrestrial lines only.

I couldn't take data from Infrapedia itself: its map needs a LinkedIn sign-in and its rules say the data can't be downloaded. But its public site index lists every network it shows, about 45 of them in the US. I checked each company's own website map to see whether the company publishes the route data itself.

**Added to your state layers**, all published by the company or a government agency:
- **Uniti / Windstream:** the biggest find, about 700,000 segments, including its national long-haul network. It also shows that a large layer I had dropped earlier as "unknown uploader" really is Uniti's own.
- **US Signal:** route files for 10 Midwest and eastern states, loaded by its own website map.
- **Southern Telecom:** it only publishes PDFs, but 8 of them contain real map coordinates. I pulled the fiber lines out of those and checked each one lands in the right city.
- **FiberLight:** its national network. You already had its Northern Virginia detail.
- **Unite Private Networks:** through Kansas City's public right-of-way permit records.
- **Midwest Fiber Networks**, and a Florida DOT project in Tampa that surveyed the telecom lines in its area.

**Not added:**
- **No public map data:** WOW, Cox, Charter, Crown Castle, ExteNet, Zayo, Arcadian and a few others only offer images, PDFs without coordinates, or maps behind a sales form.
- **An account named "geocode_Zayo":** it holds detailed Zayo data, including how many fiber strands are free, but I can't confirm it's really Zayo's, so I left it out.
- **A Midwest Fiber Networks file with "nda" in its name:** I only used the one labelled "website".

**Also fixed:** a bug in my earlier filter had dropped 3 real telecom layers. They're back in.

Each line still says who published it (`publisher`) and whether it's your hand-checked data or from the automated search (`origin`). I added a section to your methodology log and backed up the log first. The code is merged in [uvytle/HELP-ME#4](https://github.com/uvytle/HELP-ME/pull/4).

Press **Ctrl+S** in QGIS to save the project.

./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | tee "$TEMP/plains_search.txt" | head -150
import csv, re
from sources.arcgis import get_json
BOX={"Montana":(-116.1,44.3,-104.0,49.0),"Wyoming":(-111.1,40.9,-104.0,45.0),"South Dakota":(-104.1,42.4,-96.4,45.95),
     "North Dakota":(-104.1,45.9,-96.5,49.0),"Oklahoma":(-103.0,33.6,-94.4,37.0)}
TERMS='fiber OR fibre OR broadband OR telecom OR "middle mile" OR conduit OR ITS OR communication OR communications OR backbone OR network'
known={r["layer_url"].rsplit("/",1)[0] for r in csv.DictReader(open("sources/arcgis_fiber_catalog.csv",encoding="utf-8"))}
seen=set()
for st,(x0,y0,x1,y1) in BOX.items():
    hits=[]
    for kind in ("Feature Service","Map Service"):
        start=1
        while 0<start<=1000:
            r=get_json("https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/search",{"q":f'({TERMS}) type:"{kind}"',"bbox":f"{x0},{y0},{x1},{y1}","num":100,"start":start})
            for it in r["results"]:
                ext=it.get("extent") or []
                if not ext: continue
                (a,b),(c,d)=ext; cx,cy=(a+c)/2,(b+d)/2
                if not (x0<=cx<=x1 and y0<=cy<=y1): continue
                if it["id"] in seen: continue
                seen.add(it["id"])
                if not re.search(r"fib|broadband|telecom|middle|conduit|\bits\b|communic|backbone|network|cable|dark|route",(it["title"]+" "+" ".join(it.get("tags") or [])),re.I): continue
                hits.append(it)
            start=r.get("nextStart",-1)
    print(f"===== {st}: {len(hits)}")
    for it in hits:
        k="KNOWN" if (it.get("url") or "").rstrip("/") in known else "new"
        print(f"  {k:5}|{it['title'][:60]:60}|{it['owner'][:28]:28}|{it.get('url')}")
EOF

import csv, re
from sources.arcgis import get_json
known={r["layer_url"].rsplit("/",1)[0] for r in csv.DictReader(open("sources/arcgis_fiber_catalog.csv",encoding="utf-8"))}
Q={"Montana":['ConnectMT','"Montana" middle mile','"Vision Net"','MDT fiber','Blackfoot fiber','"Mid-Rivers"','Montana Opticom','Triangle Communications','Montana broadband fiber','"3 Rivers" fiber','Nemont','Montana fiber'],
   "Wyoming":['Wyoming middle mile','WYDOT fiber','WYDOT ITS','Visionary fiber','"Union Wireless"','Wyoming fiber','Wyoming broadband fiber','Silver Star fiber','"Mountain West" fiber'],
   "South Dakota":['SDN Communications','SDTA','Midco fiber','Golden West fiber','South Dakota fiber','Sioux Falls fiber','SDDOT fiber','Venture Communications','Alliance Communications fiber'],
   "North Dakota":['"Dakota Carrier Network"','STAGEnet','NDDOT fiber','NDDOT ITS','North Dakota fiber','Polar Communications','"SRT" fiber','BEK fiber','Dakota Central','North Dakota broadband'],
   "Oklahoma":['OneNet','Oklahoma middle mile','ODOT fiber','ODOT ITS','Oklahoma fiber','Dobson fiber','Pioneer Telephone fiber','Oklahoma Broadband Office','Tulsa fiber','Oklahoma City fiber','OKC fiber','Cherokee Nation fiber','Chickasaw fiber','Choctaw fiber','Oklahoma broadband fiber']}
for st,qs in Q.items():
    print("=====",st); seen=set()
    for q in qs:
        r=get_json("https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/search",{"q":f'({q}) (type:"Feature Service" OR type:"Map Service")',"num":50})
        for it in r["results"]:
            if it["id"] in seen or not it.get("url"): continue
            seen.add(it["id"])
            ext=it.get("extent") or []
            if ext:
                (a,b),(c,d)=ext
                if c<-170 or a>-60: continue
            k="KNOWN" if it["url"].rstrip("/") in known else "new"
            print(f"  {k:5}|{q[:18]:18}|{it['title'][:55]:55}|{it['owner'][:24]:24}|{it['url']}")
EOF

for q in ['MLRS rights-of-way','BLM right of way linear','BLM MLRS fiber optic','BLM rights-of-way telecommunication','"Land Use Authorizations" BLM','BLMMLRS_FiberOpticRelatedData','USFS special use telecommunication','BLM ROW grants lines']:
    r=get_json("https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/search",{"q":f'({q}) (type:"Feature Service" OR type:"Map Service")',"num":15})
    print("==",q,r["total"])
    for it in r["results"]: print("   ",it["title"][:60],"|",it["owner"][:25],"|",it.get("url"))
EOF

from sources.arcgis import get_json
import geopandas as gpd, collections
U="https://gis.blm.gov/nlsdb/rest/services/HUB/BLM_Natl_MLRS_LUA_ROW/FeatureServer/0/query"
tel="(BLM_PROD LIKE '%TEL%' OR BLM_PROD LIKE 'COMMUNICATION%')"
r=get_json(U,{"where":tel+" AND GEO_STATE='WY' AND BLM_PROD LIKE 'TELEPHONE%'","outFields":"CSE_NR,CSE_NAME,CUST_NM_SEC,CSE_WIDTH,CSE_LGTH,SRC,QLTY,CSE_DISP,RCRD_ACRS","resultRecordCount":300,"outSR":4326,"f":"geojson"})
g=gpd.GeoDataFrame.from_features(r["features"],crs=4326)
print(len(g)); print(collections.Counter(g.SRC).most_common(5)); print(collections.Counter(g.QLTY).most_common(5)); print(collections.Counter(g.CSE_DISP).most_common(5))
m=g.to_crs(5070); m["area"]=m.area; m["perim"]=m.length; m["thin"]=m.perim**2/(m.area+1)
print(m[["CSE_NAME","CUST_NM_SEC","CSE_WIDTH","CSE_LGTH","area","thin"]].head(12).to_string())
print("parts per feature:", g.geometry.apply(lambda x: len(x.geoms) if hasattr(x,'geoms') else 1).describe()[['mean','max']].to_dict())
EOF

## Project Overview

The Massachusetts Broadband Institute (MBI) announced that the 1,200-mile fiber network MassBroadband 123 is now complete. The MassBroadband 123 project consists of over 1,200 miles of fiber to connect over 120 unserved and underserved communities in western and north central Massachusetts.

## Map and Data Availability

Maps are available showing the MassBroadband 123 service area and network, including the location of fiber-optic cables and points of interconnection. The Massachusetts Broadband Institute maintains a Map Gallery at broadband.masstech.org/map-gallery with various maps related to the network.

Importantly, the MB123 middle mile has a KMZ file available at MassBroadband 123 Maps & Data. This KMZ format is useful for viewing geographic data in Google Earth and other mapping applications.

The official MBI website provides access to maps depicting the MassBroadband 123 network design, service areas, and related information about both the middle-mile fiber backbone and last-mile connection programs.

## Overview

The Connecticut Education Network (CEN) is a statewide, high-speed fiber-optic network serving the research and education community in Connecticut. Established in 2000, it was the first all-optical research and education network in the United States.

## Network Coverage

CEN operates over 2,500 optical fiber route miles across 24 hub sites bringing advanced network and technology solutions to its members throughout the state. CEN's statewide fiber optic network connects more than 1.8 million students, educators, researchers, state and municipal employees, and citizens in support of Connecticut's workforce and economic development.

## Services

CEN provides internet access, security services, and data transport to K–12 schools, higher education institutions, libraries, and municipal governments.

## Overview

OpenCape is a non-profit organization located on Cape Cod that constructed a comprehensive middle mile communications network to expand broadband access throughout Cape Cod, the Islands and the South Coast.

## Network Details

OpenCape operates 700 route miles with over 100,000 fiber miles, connecting in Boston & Providence. Over the past several years OpenCape has deployed fiber deeper into the region, expanding the network from an initial 350 miles to 650 miles of fiber, serving a growing number of Main Street businesses across the Cape.

## Network Map

You can use their map to explore current coverage areas across Cape Cod, Southeastern Massachusetts, and Rhode Island. The official network map is available at their website at https://www.opencape.org/ournetwork and https://www.opencape.org/about/network-map.

## Services

OpenCape owns and operates a state-of-the-art 100% Fiber Optic Network built to serve local governments, businesses, and residents of Southeastern MA, Cape Cod and the Islands. Broadband services are being provided over the OpenCape 100% Fiber Optic Network to more than 100 institutions, including libraries, government buildings, schools, colleges, hospitals, public safety agencies and research institutions.

NYSERNet, Inc. (New York State Education and Research Network) is a non-profit Internet service provider in New York State that mainly provides Internet access to universities, colleges, museums, health care facilities, primary and secondary schools, and research institutions.

**Network History and Development:**

NYSERNet was founded in 1986 in Troy, New York. NYSERNet's network reaches from Buffalo to New York City and was completed in 1987 as the first statewide regional IP network in the United States.

**Fiber Backbone:**

NYSERNet acquired a fiber optic path across New York State and built the next generation of the network. NYSERNet started building the New York City optical network and established Colo@32 on the Avenue of the Americas.

**Current Services:**

Nysernet provides scalable bandwidth up to 100Gb and advanced solutions like the R&E Network and Dark Fiber. NYSERNet publishes a NYC Metro Dark Fiber Network service, positioned for scalable, customizable connectivity and integrated with national and international R&E networking pathways.

content.thinking: Vision Net publishes its full Montana fiber network on its own site, while DCN's map is just a static SVG with no usable coordinates, so I'm adding Vision Net and skipping DCN. I'm also updating the state-split logic to break multi-part lines so networks crossing state borders get assigned correctly to each state they pass through.

input.command:
cd scripts/us-fiber-network && ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path("sources/carrier_files.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
s=s.replace('''    # MassBroadband 123: the state-built middle mile''','''    # Vision Net (Montana): its website's network-coverage map loads this GeoJSON.
    # The number in the filename is a build stamp and will change when Vision Net
    # updates the map; if the fetch 404s, find the new name in the page's network log.
    ("Vision Net", "carrier", "https://vision.net/network-coverage/",
     ["https://vision.net/wp-content/uploads/fiver-map-viewer-3/dist/data/kmz-folders/"
      "enabled-lines-1779911864.geojson"], ALL_LINES),
    # MassBroadband 123: the state-built middle mile''')
s=s.replace("- MassBroadband 123:","- Vision Net: the GeoJSON behind its website's coverage map.\n- MassBroadband 123:")
p.write_text(s,encoding="utf-8")
p=Path("build_dataset.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old='''    fiber = gpd.GeoDataFrame(pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), crs="EPSG:4326")
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,'''    fiber = gpd.GeoDataFrame(pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True), crs="EPSG:4326")
    # Some sources ship a whole network as one multi-part line (Vision Net is a
    # single feature spanning Montana). Split them so each piece is assigned
    # to the state it's actually in.
    fiber = fiber.explode(index_parts=False).reset_index(drop=True)
''')
p.write_text(s,encoding="utf-8")
EOF
./.venv/Scripts/python.exe -W ignore build_dataset.py --only files 2>&1 | tail -3
input.description: Add Vision Net source and explode multi-part lines before state split

content.thinking: I've found that the biggest remaining dataset in the Northeast/Plains—government-published Crown Castle, Zayo, and Lumen fiber records from Boston, Westchester County, and FDOT—is being excluded by the current rule since the carrier itself didn't publish them. This is a decision point I need your input on.

questions.question: Should government agencies' own records of Crown Castle / Zayo / Lumen lines be allowed? Examples: City of Boston's Crown Castle layer, Westchester County's Crown Castle map, and FDOT's surveyed Zayo/Level 3 lines. These are official public records, often from permits or surveys, so their source is traceable. Anonymous re-uploads would still stay out.

options.label: Allow gov't records (Recommended)
options.description: Keep Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle lines when a government agency published them from its own records (permits, right-of-way, surveys). Still exclude anonymous/third-party uploads. Adds a lot in Boston, NYC area, Florida.

options.label: Keep current rule
options.description: Only include Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle routes if the carrier itself published them (which none do). Most conservative; matches your original Lumen 'no duplication' note.

options.label: Skip

content.thinking: The state-by-state search surfaced roughly 100 new layers, many legitimate fiber/conduit datasets (Boston, Pittsburgh, Dallas County, Concord MA, Sioux Falls, Hennepin County, NoaNet Kittitas, Mono County's Digital 395, etc.), but also unrelated "conduit" results like stormwater, sewer, irrigation, and street lights. I'm adding filters to exclude those non-telecom matches.

input.command:
./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path("sources/arcgis_fiber.py"); s=p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old='''    ("title+layer", "outside US", re.compile(r"canada|coquitlam", re.I)),'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,old+'''
    # The per-state search's "conduit" term also finds non-telecom conduit:
    # stormwater/sewer/irrigation pipes, flood models, street-light conduit.
    ("title+layer", "not telecom (water/storm/lighting conduit)", re.compile(
        r"storm|sanitary|sewer|irrigat|drainage|flood|culvert|open channel|icm_model|"
        r"surcharge|capacityanalysis|\\bwater\\b|street ?light|slconduit|lighting|"
        r"electric(?!.*fib)", re.I)),
    ("title+layer", "not a route (customers/prospects)", re.compile(r"potential|customers|prospect", re.I)),''')
s=s.replace('''r"markup|missing_counts|allocation|label|indoor|\\bdetails\\b|schematic|backup"''','''r"markup|missing_counts|allocation|label|indoor|\\bdetails\\b|schematic|backup|background"''')
p.write_text(s,encoding="utf-8")
EOF
grep -n "background\"\|not telecom" sources/arcgis_fiber.py; ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "from sources import arcgis_fiber as a; a.refine_catalog()" && ./.venv/Scripts/python.exe - <<'EOF'
import csv, subprocess, io
old={r["layer_url"]:r for r in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(subprocess.run(["git","show","HEAD:scripts/us-fiber-network/sources/arcgis_fiber_catalog.csv"],capture_output=True,text=True,encoding="utf-8").stdout))}
new=list(csv.DictReader(open("sources/arcgis_fiber_catalog.csv",encoding="utf-8")))
added=[r for r in new if r["include"]=="1" and (r["layer_url"] not in old or old[r["layer_url"]]["include"]!="1")]
lost=[r for r in new if r["include"]!="1" and r["layer_url"] in old and old[r["layer_url"]]["include"]=="1"]
print("added",len(added), sum(int(r["feature_count"]) for r in added),"lost",len(lost))
for r in lost: print("  LOST",r["exclude_reason"],"|",r["title"][:50],"|",r["layer_name"][:30])
for r in sorted(added,key=lambda r:-int(r["feature_count"]))[:60]: print(f'{int(r["feature_count"]):7} | {r["publisher"][:34]:34} | {r["title"][:42]:42} | {r["layer_name"][:25]}')
EOF

"""
ArcGIS layers found by tracing the US terrestrial networks listed on
Infrapedia (infrapedia.com/terrestrialnetworks.xml, its public sitemap) back to
data the operators or public agencies publish themselves.

Infrapedia's own map is login-gated and its FAQ says its data can't be
downloaded, so we don't touch it. We only use its list of network *names* as
leads. For each lead, the carrier's own website map was opened and, where it
was an embedded ArcGIS map, traced to the public layers behind it (the same
technique used earlier for FiberLight). Title-keyword discovery misses these
because their titles don't say "fiber" (e.g. "National Core Network 6.12").

These rows are merged into the ArcGIS catalog with their publisher already
set, so they skip the automatic publisher lookup. They still go through every
other filter (content rules, the Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle rule, de-duplication).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from .arcgis import get_json

UNITI = "https://services.arcgis.com/QO7AhQX53d0m9M2s/arcgis/rest/services"
UNITI_BASIS = "carrier website: unitiwholesale.com/network-map embeds this ArcGIS map"
FIBERLIGHT_BASIS = "carrier website: fiberlight.com network coverage map embeds this ArcGIS map"
KCMO = "https://mapd.kcmo.org/kcgis/rest/services/external/FiberLayersNonKCMO/FeatureServer"
KCMO_BASIS = "public agency server (mapd.kcmo.org, City of Kansas City, MO)"

# (layer_url, dataset title, publisher, publisher_type, basis, status_guess)
SEED_LAYERS = [
    # Uniti (which merged with Windstream; Infrapedia's "Windstream core network").
    (f"{UNITI}/National_Core_Network_6_12/FeatureServer/191", "Uniti National Core Network", "Uniti", "carrier", UNITI_BASIS, "existing"),
    (f"{UNITI}/Regional_Transport_Network_6_13/FeatureServer/194", "Uniti Regional Transport Network", "Uniti", "carrier", UNITI_BASIS, "existing"),
    (f"{UNITI}/Uniti_Wholesale_Dark_Fiber/FeatureServer/74", "Uniti Wholesale Dark Fiber", "Uniti", "carrier", UNITI_BASIS, "existing"),
    (f"{UNITI}/Uniti_Wholesale_Map_Demo_4_WFL1/FeatureServer/26", "Kinetic (ex-Windstream ILEC) Dark Fiber", "Uniti", "carrier", UNITI_BASIS, "existing"),
    (f"{UNITI}/Key_Strategic_Routes_731/FeatureServer/199", "Uniti Key Strategic Routes", "Uniti", "carrier", UNITI_BASIS, "existing"),
    (f"{UNITI}/Uniti_Wholesale_Map_Demo_4_WFL1/FeatureServer/54", "Uniti Developing Routes (under review)", "Uniti", "carrier", UNITI_BASIS, "planned"),
    # FiberLight's national network (the thesis already has its Northern VA detail).
    ("https://services.arcgis.com/cmtiXjnD63zmtycz/arcgis/rest/services/FiberLightNetwork/FeatureServer/3",
     "FiberLight Network", "FiberLight", "carrier", FIBERLIGHT_BASIS, "existing"),
    # Kansas City, MO publishes other operators' fiber from its right-of-way records.
    *[(f"{KCMO}/{i}", f"KCMO right-of-way fiber: {name}", "City of Kansas City, MO", "public", KCMO_BASIS, "existing")
      for i, name in [(0, "Johnson County"), (1, "Unified Government (KCK)"), (2, "KC Scout (MoDOT/KDOT ITS)"),
                      (3, "Unite Private Networks")]],
]

# FDOT District 7's Tampa Westshore Interchange project publishes the surveyed
# existing utilities in its corridor, one layer per owner (UTEXRD_<OWNER>_<date>).
# Only telecom owners are kept; restricted carriers are removed later by the
# provenance rule like any other copy.
FDOT_D7_OWNER = "joel.wixson_fdotd7westshore"
FDOT_D7_TELECOM_RE = re.compile(
    r"^UTEXRD_(ATT|BRIGHT_HOUSE|SPECTRUM|TIME_WARNER|TECO_TELECOM|FIBERLIGHT(?:_XO_COMMUNICATIONS)?|"
    r"FRONTIER|INTERMEDIA|MCI|MFS|UNITI_FIBER|FDOT_ITS_TRAFFIC|ACSI_01|CENTURYLINK|LEVEL_3|ZAYO|"
    r"CROWN_CASTLE)(?:_(\d{8}))?")


def _fdot_d7_rows() -> list[tuple]:
    items, start = [], 1
    while start > 0:
        r = get_json("https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/search",
                     {"q": f'owner:"{FDOT_D7_OWNER}" title:UTEXRD', "num": 100, "start": start})
        items += r["results"]
        start = r.get("nextStart", -1)
    latest: dict[str, tuple[str, dict]] = {}
    for it in items:
        m = FDOT_D7_TELECOM_RE.match(it["title"])
        if not m or not it.get("url"):
            continue
        # Several owners were re-exported on different dates; keep the newest.
        if m.group(1) not in latest or (m.group(2) or "") > latest[m.group(1)][0]:
            latest[m.group(1)] = (m.group(2) or "", it)
    rows = []
    for owner, (_, it) in sorted(latest.items()):
        svc = get_json(it["url"])
        for lyr in svc.get("layers", []):
            if lyr.get("geometryType") == "esriGeometryPolyline":
                rows.append((f"{it['url'].rstrip('/')}/{lyr['id']}",
                             f"FDOT D7 Westshore surveyed utilities: {owner.replace('_', ' ').title()}",
                             "Florida DOT District 7 (Westshore Interchange project)", "public",
                             "public agency project account (hand-checked)", "existing"))
    return rows


def seed_rows() -> list[dict]:
    """Catalog rows for all seeded layers, with live feature counts."""
    rows = []
    for url, title, pub, ptype, basis, status in SEED_LAYERS + _fdot_d7_rows():
        try:
            info = get_json(url)
            count = get_json(f"{url}/query", {"where": "1=1", "returnCountOnly": "true"}).get("count", 0)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a moved layer shouldn't break the build
            print(f"    seed unavailable: {title}: {exc}")
            continue
        rows.append({
            "include": 1, "exclude_reason": "", "publisher": pub, "publisher_type": ptype,
            "publisher_basis": basis, "status_guess": status, "title": title,
            "owner": "", "layer_name": info.get("name", ""), "feature_count": count,
            "layer_url": url, "item_id": "", "seeded": "infrapedia lead",
        })
    return rows

input.new_string:
Newest on top.

## 2026-09-24 — Regional gap-filling: per-state discovery, agency copies of Lumen/Zayo/Crown allowed, BLM skipped

- **Per-state discovery.** ArcGIS search stops at 1,000 results per query, so the
  national keyword sweep was silently truncated. Discovery now also runs one
  bounding-box query per state, which more than doubled the candidates (1,316 → 3,078)
  and found e.g. City of Boston, Pittsburgh, Dallas County and Concord MA fiber. The
  catalog never drops a layer an earlier run found. New content filters handle the
  "conduit" noise this brings (storm/sewer/irrigation/street-light conduit, prospect
  lists), and a missing "backup/background" rule was restored.
- **Rule change (Vy's call):** Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle routes are now allowed when a
  *government agency* published them from its own permit/right-of-way/survey records
  (Boston, Westchester, Philadelphia, FDOT). Anonymous or other third-party copies stay
  excluded.

# Decisions log

Newest on top.

## 2026-09-24 — Infrapedia used for leads only; operator-published data traced from it

- **What:** Vy uses Infrapedia as a reference and asked for its sources. Infrapedia's map
  is login-gated and its FAQ rules out downloads, so none of its data is used. Only its
  public sitemap's list of network names is, as leads to trace to each operator's own
  website map. That added Uniti/Windstream, FiberLight, US Signal, Southern Telecom
  (GeoPDFs), Midwest Fiber Networks, Kansas City's right-of-way layers (incl. Unite
  Private Networks) and an FDOT D7 project (`carrier_maps.py`, `carrier_files.py`).
- **Judgment calls:** a public "geocode_Zayo" ArcGIS account with strand-level Zayo data
  was left out, since it's unverifiable as Zayo's and looks internal. A Midwest Fiber
  Networks KMZ with "nda" in its name was skipped in favour of the one labelled
  "website". Seeded layers still go through the content and Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle rules.
- **Southern Telecom GeoPDFs** are extracted once with QGIS's GDAL
  (`tools/extract_geopdf.py`) and the result committed, because the pip GDAL wheel has
  no PDF driver.

## 2026-09-24 — US fiber route collector: provenance rule, no railroads, data not in git

- **What:** `scripts/us-fiber-network/` gathers publicly published US fiber *route*
  geometry (mostly ArcGIS layers from cities, counties, DOTs, utilities, carriers, plus
  OpenStreetMap) and splits it by state. The output feeds the "State & Regional Fiber
  Networks" group in Vy's thesis QGIS project as `<State> (compiled)` layers.
- **Provenance rule:** keep public entities + carriers publishing their own network;
  drop consultants, Esri demo data, anonymous uploads, and Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle routes
  not published by that carrier. Vy picked this over "public only" and "everything". It
  matches the thesis log's earlier calls (Lumen's no-duplication terms, rejecting an
  untraceable Pennsylvania re-upload, rejecting Vermont's availability-snapped "routes").
  Excluded layers stay in the committed catalog CSV with a reason, so the rule can be
  revisited without re-running discovery.
- **Railroads left out** at Vy's request, even though a lot of long-haul fiber follows
  rail. Interstates are still collected as a context layer but aren't added to the map.
- **Generated data is git-ignored.** It's 1–2 GB, far past what belongs in a public
  Pages repo. The committed catalog makes a rebuild reproducible; the thesis copy lives
  in Vy's thesis folder.
- **Ruled out:** InterTubes and FiberLocator (gated/licensed), PeeringDB (AUP), Infrapedia
  (login plus no downloads). See the thesis methodology log for details.

## 2026-09-10 — Enabled entire.io CLI to capture AI session history in git

- **What:** Installed the [entire](https://entire.io) CLI and ran `entire enable`, which
  hooked into Claude Code (via `.claude/settings.json` hooks) and started capturing AI
  coding sessions as git refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/...`) linked to commits. Added
  read-only `entire` subcommands (`status`, `session`, `checkpoint`, `blame`, `why`,
  `recap`, `doctor`, `version`) to the permission allowlist so they don't prompt.
- **Why:** Requested so anyone reading this repo's history later — Vy, the SWE, or a
  future Claude session — can see not just *what* changed but the actual AI session
  that produced it, without relying on chat transcripts living elsewhere.
- **Privacy tradeoff, explicitly accepted:** by default, checkpoints sync to `origin`
  alongside code (`entire status` confirms "Checkpoints sync to: origin"). HELP-ME is
  **public**, so this means captured AI session content (prompts, tool calls) becomes
  publicly visible in git history, not just the code. This was flagged before enabling
  and the call was made deliberately to let checkpoints go public rather than route
  them to a separate private remote. If that changes, checkpoint routing is reconfigured
  via `entire configure`, not by disabling capture entirely.
- **Not yet done:** `entire login` (browser OAuth to a hosted Entire account) — that's a
  one-time human step neither I nor a future session can complete on someone else's
  behalf. Local checkpoint capture works without it; login only gates hosted features
  (cross-repo `entire activity`, semantic `entire search`, etc.).

## 2026-09-10 — Repo set up as a GitHub Pages site with worktree + PR workflow

- **What:** Made the repo public, turned on GitHub Pages (source: `main` branch, root),
  and laid out folders: site content at the repo root (`index.html`, `css/`, `js/`,
  `assets/`, `pages/`), non-site tooling under `scripts/`, and this `docs/` folder for
  memory/rationale.
- **Why:** Repo previously had no structure (a loose script + gif at root) and Pages
  wasn't enabled. The site is meant to be one page reachable at one URL, navigated via
  tabs (see `js/main.js`), not a folder-per-project layout — so the root stays the
  site's home and `docs/` is reserved purely for this log rather than doubling as the
  Pages source.
- **Workflow going forward:** feature work happens on a branch (via a git worktree),
  pushed early via a PR, reviewed by the SWE before merging to `main`. No unit tests
  required (not production software) but changes should be manually verified — opened
  in a browser, script run once — before pushing. Keep commits small and the message
  focused on *why*.
- **Moved:** `ascii_network_animation.py` + `panopticon_network.gif` → `scripts/ascii-network-animation/`
  and `assets/` respectively; the GIF is now shown on the site's Projects tab as an
  example entry.

new='''### Gap-filling: Plains (MT/WY/ND/SD/OK) and Northeast (NY/CT/MA/NJ) (2026-09-24)
- **Method change: per-state search.** ArcGIS Online stops at 1,000 results per query,
  so the original national keyword sweep was silently cut off. Discovery now also runs one
  map-bounded search per state (candidates went from 1,316 to 3,078 items). New finds
  include the City of Boston's fiber (~19k segments), Pittsburgh IT conduit, Concord MA,
  Sioux Falls traffic conduit, Dallas County, Hennepin County, Mono County's Digital 395
  backbone and more. Non-telecom "conduit" layers this surfaced (storm/sewer/irrigation,
  street-light conduit) are filtered out.
- **Sources of Infrapedia's sources, regional follow-up:**
  - **Vision Net (MT):** the GeoJSON behind its own website coverage map, i.e. its whole Montana
    network (dated Q2 2026, extends into ND).
  - **MassBroadband 123 (MA):** MBI's own KMZ of the state-built middle mile (Operational /
    Accepted / Final Review fiber, 3,210 segments, Jan 2014), recovered from the Internet
    Archive copy of MBI's since-removed "Maps & Data" page. Its "Lightower Fiber" layer was left out.
  - **NTIA (federal):** the public Enabling Middle Mile dashboard layers: 35 awarded
    routes (*planned*) and 8 awardees' existing IRU routes, nationwide.
  - **Oklahoma Broadband Office:** 19 middle-mile project routes (*planned*).
  - **Montana DOT:** Anaconda–Butte broadband routes.
- **Rule change (user's call):** Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle lines are now allowed when a
  **government agency** published them from its own records (permits, right-of-way,
  surveys), e.g. City of Boston, City of Philadelphia, FDOT, Arizona State Land Dept.
  **Refinement:** an agency's copy only counts *inside its own state*. Montgomery County,
  MD also republishes Crown Castle's *national* network (which had briefly made Connecticut
  look full), and that isn't a Maryland record, so 26,103 such out-of-state features are dropped.
- **De-duplication across datasets:** a line within 10 m of one already kept from a
  different dataset is dropped (the carrier's own copy wins, then government, then OSM),
  since agency copies of carrier networks would otherwise double-draw routes.
- **Checked and not usable:** Zayo's own site (PNG maps only), Dakota Carrier Network's
  "interactive" map (a plain SVG drawing, no coordinates), Midco's GIS server (login
  required), SD's "SDTA Fiber" layer (expansion *areas*, not routes), MuralNet's tribal
  fiber routes (login), CEN (CT), OpenCape (MA), NYSERNet (NY), NJEdge (NJ), OneNet (OK).
  None of these publish route geometry.
- **BLM right-of-way grants (skipped, user's call):** BLM's national land-use layer lists
  ~8,200 telephone/fiber-optic grants with holders (Qwest/Lumen, Union Telephone, RT
  Communications, Mid-Rivers, Triangle, 3 Rivers…). The shapes are survey-section blocks,
  not cable paths, so they were left off the route map. They could be used as an
  "approximate corridor" layer later.
- **Provenance note for Pennsylvania:** the City of Franklin, PA utility's layer includes Zito
  Media's own "Sales External" KMZ (~5,300 km statewide) alongside Venango County dark fiber.
  Zito labelled it for external distribution; it's kept, and `attributes.FolderPath` shows it.
- **Honest limit:** WY, ND, SD and CT remain thin because almost nothing is published there.
  The providers (e.g. Union Telephone, DCN, SDN, CEN) show only images or nothing. The
  public-records-request route noted above (state DOT fiber permit inventories) is the
  most promising way to fill them.

'''

EOF

## What

- **Per-state discovery.** Discovery also runs one bounding-box ArcGIS search per state. Candidates went from 1,316 to 3,078 items and the catalog grew from 632 to 733 included layers. Layers found by earlier runs are never dropped.
- **Stricter content filters.** Adds filters for non-telecom conduit (storm/sewer/irrigation/street-light) and prospect lists, and restores the lost `backup|background` rule.
- **New sources:**
  - Vision Net's coverage-map GeoJSON (MT).
  - MassBroadband 123, MBI's KMZ via the Internet Archive (MA).
  - NTIA Enabling Middle Mile routes (federal).
  - Oklahoma Broadband Office middle-mile routes.
  - Montana DOT Anaconda–Butte routes.
- **Provenance rule.** Government agencies' own records of Lumen/Zayo/Crown Castle lines are allowed, but only inside the agency's state (`publishers.JURISDICTION`).
- **Cross-dataset de-duplication.** A 10 m check in the state split; the carrier's own copy wins, then government, then OSM.
- **Fix.** Sources whose only attribute is a lowercase `name` lost their publisher fields.

## Why

Vy flagged thin coverage in MT/WY/ND/SD/OK and NY/CT/MA/NJ and asked to go further up Infrapedia's source chain. The main cause was that the national ArcGIS search was silently cut off at 1,000 results per query.

The agency-records rule was Vy's decision. The jurisdiction limit was added after a Maryland county's copy of Crown Castle's national network made Connecticut look full. BLM right-of-way grants were considered and skipped (Vy's call): they're survey sections, not cable paths. Details are in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and the README.

## Verified

- **Full build.** Discovery, then download (728/729 layers), then the files layer and the de-duplicated state split, all ran.
- **Target-state results:**
  - Massachusetts: 575 → 29,406
  - New York: 15,620 → 14,342 (after removing out-of-state agency copies and duplicates)
  - South Dakota: 274 → 8,114
  - North Dakota: 150 → 1,438
  - Montana: Vision Net covers the state
- **Spot checks:**
  - The Connecticut "solid block" traced to Montgomery County MD's national Crown Castle copy and is now dropped (26,103 out-of-state features).
  - The Pennsylvania grid look is just rendering; Kinetic lines aren't axis-aligned.
  - Vision Net's disappearance was traced to the lowercase `name` attribute and fixed.
- **In QGIS.** Merged into Vy's thesis project: 52 state layers, 1,408,072 features.

content.text:
Your map now has 1,408,072 fiber segments across 52 state layers, with more coverage in Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, Oklahoma, Massachusetts and New York. Wyoming, Connecticut and New Jersey are still thin, because almost nothing about them is published anywhere I could find.

**Zayo, as you asked:** Zayo publishes no route data, only flat PNG images on its website. Much of its network in the Plains came from Touch America (the old Montana Power fiber company). Those lines show up in the federal land agency's (BLM's) right-of-way records, but only as blocks of survey sections, not the actual cable path, so you chose to leave them out.

**New sources**, all published by the network owner or a government agency:
- **Vision Net:** its whole Montana fiber network, taken from the data behind its own website map.
- **MassBroadband 123:** Massachusetts' state-built fiber network. The file had been taken off the state's website, so I got it from the Internet Archive's saved copy.
- **Federal and state grant routes:** the federal Middle Mile grant routes (NTIA), the Oklahoma Broadband Office's routes, and a Montana DOT route set.
- **About 100 more city and county layers,** such as Boston, Pittsburgh, Sioux Falls and Concord MA. The earlier search had been cut off at 1,000 results per query; searching each state separately found them.

**Changes to the rules:**
- **Your new rule:** government records of Crown Castle, Zayo and Lumen lines are now included, but only inside that agency's own state. Without that limit, a Maryland county's copy of Crown Castle's national network made Connecticut look full of fiber, and it isn't that county's record.
- **Duplicates:** when two sources draw the same line, only one is kept.

**Target states now:**

| State | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Massachusetts | 575 | 29,406 |
| New York | 15,620 | 14,342 (lost copies from outside NY and duplicates, gained Boston-style city data) |
| Oklahoma | ~26,000 | 23,634 (duplicates removed; state middle-mile routes added) |
| South Dakota | 274 | 8,114 |
| North Dakota | 150 | 1,438 |
| Montana | 1,216 | 1,676 (Vision Net's long lines now cross the whole state) |
| Wyoming | 187 | 271 |
| New Jersey | 668 | 667 |
| Connecticut | 300 | 318 |

**Checked but nothing usable there:** Dakota Carrier Network (its map is a plain drawing with no coordinates), Midco (needs a login), and CEN, OpenCape, NYSERNet, NJEdge and OneNet (no route data published).

**One provenance note:** in Pennsylvania, the City of Franklin's utility layer includes Zito Media's own map file labelled "Sales External", about 5,300 km. I kept it, and each line records that it came from that file.

The most promising way to fill the thin states is still the one your log already names: a public-records request to each state's DOT for its fiber permit maps.

I added a section to your methodology log and backed up the old version first. The code is merged in [uvytle/HELP-ME#5](https://github.com/uvytle/HELP-ME/pull/5). Press **Ctrl+S** in QGIS to save the project.
